statement: The supplied sources genuinely contain nothing to derive; unit norm normalization defines the normalized vector û of a non-zero vector u as the unit vector in the direction of u: û = u / ‖u‖ = (u₁ / ‖u‖, u₂ / ‖u‖, ..., uₙ / ‖u‖), where ‖u‖ is the norm (or length) of u and u = (u₁, u₂, ..., uₙ).

symbols.meaning: i-th scalar component of vector u
normalized vector (unit vector in the direction of u)

properties.property: The norm of the normalized vector is 1 (‖û‖ = 1)
properties.why: the sum of squared components divided by the squared norm evaluates to 1 under the square root

properties.property: A unit vector represents directions, such as normal directions
properties.why: it isolates directional orientation by scaling the vector to unit length

properties.property: Unit vectors can form a basis for a vector space
properties.why: every vector in the space may be written as a linear combination of unit vectors

properties.property: Standard Cartesian basis unit vectors are mutually orthogonal (ê_i · ê_j = δ_ij)
properties.why: the coordinate axes are mutually perpendicular

assumptions.breaks_when: u is the zero vector, which results in division by zero since ‖0‖ = 0

assumptions.assumption: The vector u belongs to a normed vector space with an associated norm ‖·‖
assumptions.breaks_when: the underlying space lacks a defined norm or length function

failure_modes.signature: Division by zero / undefined normalized vector
failure_modes.cause: Attempting to normalize a vector with zero length (‖u‖ = 0)

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so unit_norm_normalization is recorded as a definition
